g.title: PACK
g.text: 11.1 V nominal, 12.6 V full, 10.5 V floor. No divider, no alarm: 30-minute timer, then meter it. A pack that reads 6–7 V is dead: never charge it.

g.title: W_PACK
g.text: HOOVO T-plug → the deck plug (pack half of the OliRC extension)

g.title: PLUG
g.text: Deans pull-plug on the deck (OliRC 14 AWG extension) = the E-STOP
The mating pair sits at the deck's rear corner where a hand can reach it. Pulling it apart kills everything on the pack side; the Pi keeps running on the bank.

g.title: W_LEAD
g.text: deck plug → shield terminal (rover half of the OliRC extension)

g.title: SHIELD_PWR
g.text: CNC Shield v3 — power screw terminal (the only pack splice)

Two wires per screw: the 14 AWG pack lead and the 22 AWG XL4015 input wire, twisted together before insertion, tug-tested. 1000 µF 25 V electrolytic across VMOT/GND at the terminal, stripe (−) to GND.

g.title: W_XL_IN
g.text: second wire in each shield power screw

g.title: XL4015
g.text: HiLetgo XL4015 5 A buck — trim OUT to 5.0 V

HiLetgo board: four big solder pads, IN+/IN− at the coil end, OUT+/OUT− at the other — tin them and solder the 22 AWG wires (no screw terminals). Set 5.00 V on the meter with nothing on OUT (pot turns counter-clockwise to lower). 4 A continuous derated. 5.0 V (not 6) so the fan can share this rail; the MG996R runs 4.8–7.2 V.

g.title: W_SERVO
g.text: 5.0 V rail into the PCA9685 terminal; OUT− → the PCA9685 GND terminal is the return for servo, fan and ESP32

g.title: PCA_PWR
g.text: The big 2-pin terminal at the end of the board = the 5.0 V rail in. Every channel header's middle (V+) and bottom (GND) pin is bussed to it — that is how the fan gets its 5 V.

g.title: PCA_CH15
g.text: PCA9685 channel 15 header — used as a 5 V tap
Only V+ and GND are used: the fan's red to V+, black to GND. PWM pin stays empty.

g.title: FAN
g.text: 40 mm 5 V fan on the driver heatsinks
5 V 0.15 A (listing). Plugs onto the PCA9685's channel-15 V+/GND pins.

g.title: BANK
g.text: USB power bank 5 V / 3 A (logic island)
Genuine 3 A bank. Cable ≤ 0.2 m with 22 AWG or heavier power conductors (a short '3 A fast-charge' cable). Powers ONLY the Pi; the Pi powers the R4, the hub, the adapters, the radars and the webcam.

g.title: PI_PWR
g.text: Under-voltage warning at 4.63 V. Early Pi 4 (rev 1.1) needs an A-to-C or non-e-marked cable.
